preconditions.description: The target sum is an integer between 1 and 10^6 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: root is None or (hasattr(root, 'data') and isinstance(root.data, int))
preconditions.description: The root is either None or a valid tree node with an integer data field.

preconditions.expression: root is None or (hasattr(root, 'left') and hasattr(root, 'right'))
preconditions.description: If root exists, it has left and right child attributes.

postconditions.description: The return value is a list of paths.

postconditions.expression: all(isinstance(path, list) and all(isinstance(node_val, int) for node_val in path) for path in return_value)
postconditions.description: Each path in the result is a list of integers representing node values.

postconditions.expression: all(sum(path) == sum for path in return_value)
postconditions.description: The sum of node values in every returned path equals the target sum.
Every returned path contains at least one node.

postconditions.expression: all(all(node_val in [root.data] if root else [] or (root.left.data if root and root.left else None) or (root.right.data if root and root.right else None) for node_val in path) for path in return_value)
postconditions.description: Every node value in a returned path corresponds to an actual node in the tree.

postconditions.expression: all(all(path[i] == path[i+1] or (path[i] in [root.data] if root else []) or (path[i+1] in [root.data] if root else []) for i in range(len(path)-1)) for path in return_value)
postconditions.description: Each path represents a valid sequence of nodes starting from the root and following parent-child links.

postconditions.expression: all(all(path[0] == root.data if root else False for path in return_value)
postconditions.description: Every path starts with the root node's value.

postconditions.expression: all(all(path[i+1] in [child.data for child in [root.left, root.right] if child] for i in range(len(path)-1)) for path in return_value)
postconditions.description: Each subsequent node in a path is a direct child of the previous node.
